questions.stem: Evaluate the integral ∫(x² dx) / (x³ + 1) from 0 to 2.
questions.solution: Using trig substitution with x = tan(θ), dx = sec²(θ)dθ, the integral becomes ∫(tan²(θ)sec²(θ)dθ) / (tan³(θ) + 1). This simplifies to ∫(sec⁴(θ)dθ) / (sec³(θ)). Integrating, we get ∫(sec(θ)dθ) from π/4 to arctan(2) = ln|sec(θ) + tan(θ)| evaluated from π/4 to arctan(2) = ln(sqrt(5) + 2) - ln(sqrt(2) + 1) = π/2.
questions.explanation: The integral is solved using trigonometric substitution and evaluating the resulting integral with respect to θ or π.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be not recognizing that dx becomes sec²(θ)dθ, leading to an incorrect result.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral ∫(sin(x) dx) / (1 + cos²(x)) from 0 to π.
questions.solution: Using trig substitution with x = 2arctan(t), dx = 2/(1 + t²)dt, the integral becomes ∫(sin(2arctan(t)) * 2/(1 + t²)dθ) / (1 + cos²(2arctan(t))). This simplifies to ∫(2t/(1 + t²)dθ) / (1 + (1 - t²)/(1 + t²)). Integrating, we get ∫(2tdθ) from 0 to 1 = π/4.
questions.explanation: The integral is solved using trigonometric substitution and evaluating the resulting integral with respect to θ or π.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be not recognizing that dx becomes 2/(1 + t²)dt, leading to an incorrect result.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral ∫(cos(x) dx) / (sin²(x) + 4) from -π/2 to π/2.
questions.solution: Using trig substitution with x = arctan(2t), dx = 2/(1 + 4t²)dt, the integral becomes ∫(cos(arctan(2t)) * 2/(1 + 4t²)dθ) / ((sin(arctan(2t)))² + 4). This simplifies to ∫(2tdθ) from -1/√3 to 1/√3 = 0.
questions.explanation: The integral is solved using trigonometric substitution and evaluating the resulting integral with respect to θ or π. The limits of integration yield an odd function, which results in a zero value.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral ∫(x³ dx) / (x⁴ + 1) from -1 to 1.
questions.solution: Using trig substitution with x = tan(θ), dx = sec²(θ)dθ, the integral becomes ∫(tan³(θ)sec²(θ)dθ) / (tan⁴(θ) + 1). This simplifies to ∫(sec⁵(θ)dθ) / (sec³(θ)). Integrating, we get ∫(sec²(θ)dθ) from -π/4 to π/4 = ln|sec(θ) + tan(θ)| evaluated from -π/4 to π/4 = ln(sqrt(2) + 1) - ln(sqrt(2) - 1) = π/2.
